current_unit: Task 12: Node 24 in CI and an engines floor
notes: Task 11 (bump Forge 7.4 -> 7.11 ahead of Electron) completed cleanly this firing. Step 1: npm i -D of the four @electron-forge/{cli,maker-dmg,maker-zip,plugin-webpack} packages, landed at ^7.11.2, Electron itself untouched (^32.0.0). Step 2: npx vitest run + npx tsc --noEmit both green -- 86/86 files, 1253/1253 tests, matching the Task 10 baseline exactly (docs/plans/electron32-test-baseline.txt), once `npm run install:companion` was run (this firing started from a fresh checkout; without that step tests/companion-defs.test.ts fails to resolve @companion-module/base, which is the plan's documented pre-existing Out-of-Scope gap, not a Forge regression -- confirmed by reproducing the full green baseline after running the install script CI itself relies on). Step 3 (`npx electron-forge package --platform darwin --arch arm64`) initially failed with ENOENT on lstat './cloudflared' -- investigated and judged this an environment-limitation, not a Forge/Electron incompatibility: forge.config.ts bundles './cloudflared' as an extraResource, that directory is gitignored, and CI populates it via a dedicated 'Download cloudflared binary' step (.github/workflows/build-release.yml) that never ran in this sandbox -- unrelated to Forge version and would fail identically on Forge 7.4. To get a real positive signal rather than just an environment-limitation excuse, created a throwaway placeholder ./cloudflared/cloudflared-darwin-arm64 binary and reran packaging: it completed end-to-end (copying files, preparing native deps, finalizing package) and produced a genuine out/PConAir-darwin-arm64/PConAir.app -- so Forge 7.11 packaging on Electron 32 is confirmed working, cross-platform from this Linux x86_64 container. Placeholder and out/ deleted after verification, not committed. Step 4: committed package.json + package-lock.json as 901d531 with the above verification detail in the commit body. No native-binding/code-signing/notarization work was involved in Task 11 itself (that's Task 14, the Electron bump), so no pause-before-native-work consideration applied here. free_reset_available untouched at true -- ordinary clean unit completion, nothing time-sensitive.
